gcoHmac.description: Request-bound HMAC envelope minted by the API Gateway proxy Lambdas (`x-gco-signature-version`, `x-gco-timestamp`, `x-gco-nonce`, `x-gco-signature`): the signature covers the method, exact path and query, body digest, timestamp and nonce under the shared signing key from Secrets Manager. Verified by `gco/services/auth_middleware.py`; a failure is a 403. Original caller identity is authenticated upstream by API Gateway IAM.
gcoHmac.name: x-gco-signature

info.description: The HTTP surface of the internal ALB that fronts a GCO region: the Kubernetes Gateway `gco-system/gco-gateway` (GatewayClass `gco-aws-alb`, implemented by `gateway.k8s.aws/alb`, the AWS Load Balancer Controller) with one HTTPS:443 listener. Its HTTPRoute `gco-routes` sends each request to a Service by longest path prefix; every operation below is one a backend Service serves *and* the route delivers to it, tagged with that Service and annotated with the winning rule (`x-gco-route`). The ALB is `internal` and answers only the API Gateway proxy Lambdas (over Global Accelerator or from the regional bridge's VPC), which sign every request with the HMAC envelope (`x-gco-signature` and companions) that the services verify on every path except `/api/v1/health`, `/healthz`, `/metrics`, `/readyz`. The ALB terminates TLS with a deployment-local certificate and re-encrypts to a TLS proxy sidecar on each pod; the service documents describe the same operations as their applications see them.
info.title: GCO Cluster Gateway (internal ALB)

get.description:
The validation policy this region actually enforces, as deployed.

Answers "will this cluster admit the job I am about to pay to run?"
before submission, so a policy conflict surfaces at plan time instead of
after a region has been provisioned and billed.

Reads the live ``ManifestProcessor`` instance rather than any config file.
A local ``cdk.json`` is the *input* to a deploy, not the state of one:
the cluster may have been deployed from a different checkout, and CDK
augments ``trusted_registries`` with the project's own ECR hostnames at
synth time, so the effective allowlist is strictly larger than the
configured one.

Three layers govern admission and all three are reported:

1. ``policy`` — the front-door checks the manifest processor and the SQS
   queue processor both apply (they read the same env vars, so neither
   submission path is a bypass).
2. ``cluster_enforcement.limit_ranges`` — per-container ceilings.
3. ``cluster_enforcement.resource_quotas`` — namespace aggregate ceilings.

A manifest must clear all three. Layers 2 and 3 are read live from the
Kubernetes API and degrade to ``status="unavailable"`` rather than
failing the whole response.

schema.title: Response Get Job Validation Policy Api V1 Policy Get
